title: Thermally Activated Long-Range Entanglement from Non-Abelian Conservation Laws
abstract: Thermal noise ordinarily suppresses quantum entanglement. We show that a strong non-Abelian conservation law can convert local thermal fluctuations into an unbounded operational resource. For a broad class of finite-range $SU(2)$-invariant spin chains restricted to the global-singlet sector, an explicit representation-space protocol yields $Y_N=\frac12\log_2 N+O_β(1)$, and hence $E_{\mathrm{D}}\geq Y_N$, throughout a finite high-temperature interval. Local thermal fluctuations produce subsystem spins $j\sim\sqrt N$, whose globally locked irreducible representations contain $\log_2(2j+1)\sim\frac12\log_2N$ ebits. An exactly solvable dimer chain exhibits a sharper effect: its zero-temperature state is unentangled across the cut, whereas every fixed $T>0$ produces $E_{\mathrm{D}}=\frac{1}{2}\log_2 N+C(T)+o(1)$, with crossover scale $T_*(N)\simΔ/\ln N$. Exact diagonalization of a nonintegrable chain is consistent with the predicted scaling. Thus heating can activate system-size-diverging distillable entanglement across a macroscopic bipartition when thermalization is confined by a non-Abelian conservation law.
summary: The paper demonstrates that imposing a strong non-Abelian conservation law on a spin chain allows local thermal noise to generate system-size-diverging distillable entanglement. Using advanced techniques from representation theory and QBP, the authors prove this scaling holds exactly for certain models like the dimer chain. This shows that symmetry can stabilize quantum correlations against thermal decoherence.
main_problem: The study investigates whether local thermal fluctuations can generate system-size-diverging distillable entanglement when the thermalization process is constrained by a strong non-Abelian conservation law.
main_result: Strong non-Abelian symmetry allows local thermal noise to activate an operational resource, leading to distillable entanglement scaling as $E_{\mathrm{D}} \sim  rac{1}{2} \log_2 N$.
method: The authors employ representation-space protocols and advanced techniques like Quantum Belief Propagation (QBP) combined with saddle-point approximations to derive asymptotic bounds on entanglement.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on finite-range SU(2)-invariant spin chains, particularly using the exactly solvable dimer chain model. The system is analyzed under thermal evolution governed by $e^{- eta H}$.
key_observables: Distillable Entanglement ($E_{\mathrm{D}}$), lower bound entanglement measure ($Y_N$), and the twisted partition function $f_{n, eta}(g)$.
important_parameters: Temperature ($ eta$ or $T>0$), system size ($N$), and the crossover scale $T^*(N) \sim \Delta / \ln N$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on bounding errors using techniques like Haar averaging approximations in QBP, and establishing asymptotic limits for large systems.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate that entanglement ($	ext{ED}$) grows logarithmically with $N$ at fixed $T>0$, confirming the predicted scaling $ rac{1}{2} \log_2 N$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing a lower bound on entanglement using representation theory, then applying QBP and saddle-point methods to derive asymptotic bounds for the partition function, culminating in exact results for the dimer chain.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical understanding of how symmetry constraints can fundamentally alter thermal physics, turning expectedly finite entanglement into an unbounded resource relevant for quantum information processing.
